## Engineering Task Shape Analysis — `asahilinux/m1n1` @ `7c7716b`

m1n1 is an AArch64 bootloader / hypervisor / research platform for Apple Silicon. The stratum is `policy_control` — code that governs which hardware capabilities are enabled, which security policies are enforced, and how the firmware interface is negotiated. Below are the task shapes evidenced by the code at the cutoff revision.

---

### 1. Feature

**Primary evidence: multiple, largely independent.**

**a. Hypervisor subsystem** (`src/hv*.c`, `src/hv_asm.S`)

The entire `hv_*` cluster — stage-2 page table management in [`src/hv_vm.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/hv_vm.c), exception interception in [`src/hv_exc.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/hv_exc.c), virtio device emulation in [`src/hv_virtio.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/hv_virtio.c), a vUART in `src/hv_vuart.c`, and AIC trap routing in `src/hv_aic.c` — constitute a coherent feature: a thin hypervisor that runs macOS or XNU as an EL1 guest while intercepting MMIO and system-register accesses. The `HCR_EL2` flag composition in [`hv_init()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/hv.c?L56-L77) (`HCR_E2H|HCR_RW|HCR_VM|HCR_AMO|HCR_TEA`) reveals deliberate VHE-mode design, not an adaptation of an existing driver.

**b. GoFetch mitigation subsystem** (`src/mitigations.c`, `src/mitigations.h`)

[`mitigations_configure()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/mitigations.c?L47-L66) and [`mitigations_perform()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/mitigations.c?L90-L109) introduce a named, configurable security mitigation framework. `patch_gofetch()` sets `HID11_DISABLE_DMP` to disable the Data-Memory-dependent Prefetcher on M1/M2 family CPUs — a new, self-contained capability triggered by boot policy, not a correction to prior logic.

**c. VirtIO-over-MMIO device emulation** (`src/hv_virtio.c`)

The [`struct virtio_dev`/`virtio_q`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/hv_virtio.c) types plus descriptor-ring wiring implement a fully new abstraction — a transport for exposing host I/O to a guest — not reachable by any prior driver subsystem in the tree.

**d. ISP initialization** (`src/isp.c`, `src/isp.h`)

[`isp_init()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/isp.c?L49-L60) brings up the Image Signal Processor DART mapping, including an IOVA base split for T6020+ (`0x10000000000`). This is a new peripheral driver with no analogous file family in the tree.

**e. EARLY_PROXY_TIMEOUT boot-policy hook** (`src/main.c`, `config.h`)

The [`run_actions()` block](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/main.c?L72-L140) gated on `EARLY_PROXY_TIMEOUT` and `lp_sip0 == 127` introduces a policy-aware early USB proxy mode triggered by a specific Secure Boot policy value (`sip0`). This is a distinct bootloader feature, not a bug fix or configuration tweak.

---

### 2. Localized Bug Fix

**Evidence: scattered, embedded in chicken-bit files and comments.**

In [`src/chickens/firestorm.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/chickens/firestorm.c?L6-L55) each `reg_set`/`reg_mask` call corresponds to a named errata or silicon bug:

- `HID0_FETCH_WIDTH_DISABLE | HID0_CACHE_FUSION_DISABLE`: *"Cross-beat Crypto ICache fusion is not disabled for branch unconditional recoded instruction"* — a targeted silicon erratum fix.
- `HID7_FORCE_NONSPEC_IF_STEPPING`: speculative-execution fence for a specific CPU stepping.

Similarly in [`src/chickens/everest.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/chickens/everest.c?L106-L108), the comment `/* This is new to M3 and i have no idea what it is yet */` on `reg_set(s3_0_c15_c2_3, BIT(3))` marks a known-necessary but not-yet-understood workaround — a localized fix applied empirically.

Each `init_*` function in `src/chickens/` is itself a bundle of localized bug fixes, not a feature: it applies bit-level patches to implementation-defined registers to correct per-revision CPU behavior. The dispatch table in [`src/chickens.c:midr_parts[]`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/chickens.c?L124-L168) routes each MIDR part to its fix set.

**Evidence: modest, localized.**

[`src/cpufreq.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/cpufreq.c) uses a `struct cluster_t` / `struct feat_t` table-driven approach to abstract p-state manipulation across a wide range of SoCs (S5L8960X through T6040). The `chip_id`-keyed `switch` in `pstate_reg_to_pstate()` is a data-table-over-conditionals idiom suggesting a prior per-SoC branching structure was consolidated. This is a mild refactor — same policy semantics, different structure.

[`src/chickens.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/chickens.c?L36-L42) introduces `struct midr_part_info` with a function pointer `init`, replacing what would otherwise be a large `switch` in `init_cpu()`. This consolidation of CPU identification and initialization is a structural refactor of the per-CPU policy-application path.

### 4. Test Generation

**Evidence: very thin at the cutoff.**

[`tests/python/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/tree/tests/python) contains only `tests/python/.gitkeep` and a `test_proxyclient/` subdirectory (no content visible at this revision). `pytest.ini` and `requirements.ini` are present at the root, confirming test infrastructure is scaffolded but the test corpus is near-empty. **Ambiguity**: it is unclear whether this represents an in-progress test generation task or merely a placeholder skeleton (see section 7).

---

### 5. Dependency Migration

**Evidence: one clear instance.**

The `rust/` subtree ([`rust/Cargo.toml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/rust/Cargo.toml), [`rust/src/lib.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/rust/src/lib.rs)) represents the introduction of Rust as a second implementation language alongside C. `lib.rs` uses `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1` (`Makefile` line 76), `no_std + alloc`, and a custom `DLMalloc` global allocator. The GPU init-data computation is delegated to Rust (`rust_gpu_initdata_size()` called from [`src/kboot_gpu.c:41`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/kboot_gpu.c?L41-L42)) while the C side handles board bringup. This is a dependency migration in the sense of a language/runtime dependency boundary being formally established — the existing dlmalloc C library is now wrapped/replaced per-allocator in Rust.

---

### 6. Documentation / Configuration

**Evidence: explicit.**

[`config.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/config.h) is a pure configuration surface: `USE_FB`, `FB_SILENT_MODE`, `EARLY_PROXY_TIMEOUT`, `BRINGUP`, `NO_DISPLAY`, `TARGET`, `USE_DEBUG_USB` — all commented-out knobs that shape build behavior. The `RELEASE` preprocessor block condenses release-time policy choices. This file is a documentation/configuration task shape: its purpose is to communicate and expose tunable policy to build operators, not to implement behavior.

[`src/soc.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/soc.h) is similarly a documentation artifact — it maps human-readable SoC names to chip IDs and UART base addresses across the entire Apple Silicon family through M5, with no logic.

[`AGENTS.md`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/AGENTS.md) (one line: forbids AI tool usage) is a policy document, not code.

---

### 7. Boilerplate

**Evidence: test infrastructure scaffolding.**

`tests/python/.gitkeep`, `pytest.ini`, `requirements.ini`, and `requirements.txt` constitute test-framework boilerplate: directory placeholders and configuration stubs that set up a test harness without containing tests. This is distinct from test generation (which implies actual test authorship).

---

### 8. Architectural Scaffolding

**Evidence: two instances.**

**a. Per-CPU feature table** (`src/chickens.c`, `src/midr.h`, `src/chickens.h`)

`struct midr_part_info` with `features` pointer to `struct midr_part_features` and an `init` function pointer is architectural scaffolding: it establishes the extensible skeleton into which new CPU variants are registered. The `features_m4` entry with `// XXX figure out what features are actually available on M4` and `SLEEP_NONE // XXX probably new mode required` explicitly signals that M4+ entries are stubs awaiting population — the shape is infrastructure, not a complete feature.

**b. Mitigation dispatch table** (`src/mitigations.c`)

`struct mitigation` with `apply_patch`, `vulnerable`, `mitigate`, `mitigated` fields, and the single-element `mitigations[]` array, is a framework deliberately over-engineered relative to a single fix. The comment on `cpus_gofetch[]` — `/* This table is complete, do not add newer CPUs */` — confirms the scaffolding intent: the table-plus-dispatcher pattern is there to accept future mitigations without restructuring.

**c. Rust/C FFI boundary** (`rust/src/lib.rs`, `src/kboot_gpu.c`)

The `extern "C"` bridge (`rust_gpu_initdata_size`, `flush_and_reboot`) is architectural scaffolding that establishes the FFI contract for delegating computation-heavy or safety-critical paths to Rust while keeping board bringup in C.

---

### 9. Cleanup

**Evidence: weak, scattered.**

The `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` guards in [`src/kboot_t6020_compat.c:8-22`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/kboot_t6020_compat.c?L8-L22) protect a string-pair table from formatter destruction — a minor code hygiene annotation. The `UNUSED(rev)` calls in `everest.c` and other chicken files suppress warnings from unused parameters without altering behavior. These are small cleanup touches embedded in otherwise feature/fix commits, not standalone cleanup tasks.

---

### Taxonomy Refinement Proposals

Two situations in this codebase do not fit cleanly into the existing taxonomy:

**A. Silicon errata workaround** (sub-type of localized bug fix)

The `src/chickens/` files apply bit-field patches to undocumented implementation-specific registers based on CPU part ID and revision. This is technically a localized bug fix, but the bug is in the silicon, not in software, and the fix is arrived at empirically or via Apple-internal guidance (many bits lack public documentation — e.g., `HID16_SPAREBIT0`, unnamed `s3_0_c15_c2_4` registers). A distinct sub-category — **silicon errata application** — would more precisely capture this shape, since it implies: (a) the defect is not in the repository's own code, (b) the fix has no test coverage by definition (no way to probe silicon without the workaround present), and (c) correctness evidence is observation-based rather than proof-based.

**B. Reverse-engineering scaffolding** (proposed new category)

[`proxyclient/hv/trace_*.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/tree/proxyclient/hv) (26 files: `trace_agx.py`, `trace_dart.py`, `trace_dcp.py`, `trace_nvme.py`, etc.) and `proxyclient/m1n1/trace/` constitute a category that none of the eight existing labels captures well. These files set up MMIO intercept handlers in the hypervisor to decode and print hardware register traffic. They are not tests (no assertions), not documentation (live instrumentation), not features (no new capability delivered to end users), not refactors. The closest label is `architectural scaffolding`, but the intent is research/observation, not extensibility. A proposed label: **reverse-engineering instrumentation** — tasks whose output is knowledge about undocumented hardware behavior rather than functional software capability.

[`config.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/config.h) is a pure configuration surface: `USE_FB`, `FB_SILENT_MODE`, `EARLY_PROXY_TIMEOUT`, `BRINGUP`, `NO_DISPLAY`, `TARGET`, `USE_DEBUG_USB` — all commented-out knobs that shape build behavior. The `RELEASE` preprocessor block condenses release-time policy choices. This file is a documentation/configuration task shape: its purpose is to communicate and expose tunable policy to build operators, not to implement behavior.

[`src/soc.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/soc.h) is similarly a documentation artifact — it maps human-readable SoC names to chip IDs and UART base addresses across the entire Apple Silicon family through M5, with no logic.

[`AGENTS.md`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/AGENTS.md) (one line: forbids AI tool usage) is a policy document, not code.

---

### 7. Boilerplate

**Evidence: test infrastructure scaffolding.**

`tests/python/.gitkeep`, `pytest.ini`, `requirements.ini`, and `requirements.txt` constitute test-framework boilerplate: directory placeholders and configuration stubs that set up a test harness without containing tests. This is distinct from test generation (which implies actual test authorship).

---

### 8. Architectural Scaffolding

**Evidence: two instances.**

**a. Per-CPU feature table** (`src/chickens.c`, `src/midr.h`, `src/chickens.h`)

`struct midr_part_info` with `features` pointer to `struct midr_part_features` and an `init` function pointer is architectural scaffolding: it establishes the extensible skeleton into which new CPU variants are registered. The `features_m4` entry with `// XXX figure out what features are actually available on M4` and `SLEEP_NONE // XXX probably new mode required` explicitly signals that M4+ entries are stubs awaiting population — the shape is infrastructure, not a complete feature.

**b. Mitigation dispatch table** (`src/mitigations.c`)

`struct mitigation` with `apply_patch`, `vulnerable`, `mitigate`, `mitigated` fields, and the single-element `mitigations[]` array, is a framework deliberately over-engineered relative to a single fix. The comment on `cpus_gofetch[]` — `/* This table is complete, do not add newer CPUs */` — confirms the scaffolding intent: the table-plus-dispatcher pattern is there to accept future mitigations without restructuring.

**c. Rust/C FFI boundary** (`rust/src/lib.rs`, `src/kboot_gpu.c`)

The `extern "C"` bridge (`rust_gpu_initdata_size`, `flush_and_reboot`) is architectural scaffolding that establishes the FFI contract for delegating computation-heavy or safety-critical paths to Rust while keeping board bringup in C.

---

### 9. Cleanup

**Evidence: weak, scattered.**

The `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` guards in [`src/kboot_t6020_compat.c:8-22`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/blob/src/kboot_t6020_compat.c?L8-L22) protect a string-pair table from formatter destruction — a minor code hygiene annotation. The `UNUSED(rev)` calls in `everest.c` and other chicken files suppress warnings from unused parameters without altering behavior. These are small cleanup touches embedded in otherwise feature/fix commits, not standalone cleanup tasks.

---

### Taxonomy Refinement Proposals

Two situations in this codebase do not fit cleanly into the existing taxonomy:

**A. Silicon errata workaround** (sub-type of localized bug fix)

The `src/chickens/` files apply bit-field patches to undocumented implementation-specific registers based on CPU part ID and revision. This is technically a localized bug fix, but the bug is in the silicon, not in software, and the fix is arrived at empirically or via Apple-internal guidance (many bits lack public documentation — e.g., `HID16_SPAREBIT0`, unnamed `s3_0_c15_c2_4` registers). A distinct sub-category — **silicon errata application** — would more precisely capture this shape, since it implies: (a) the defect is not in the repository's own code, (b) the fix has no test coverage by definition (no way to probe silicon without the workaround present), and (c) correctness evidence is observation-based rather than proof-based.

**B. Reverse-engineering scaffolding** (proposed new category)

[`proxyclient/hv/trace_*.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/asahilinux-m1n1@7c7716b6a196c7e601f9f22bb8af335c1b8173ce/-/tree/proxyclient/hv) (26 files: `trace_agx.py`, `trace_dart.py`, `trace_dcp.py`, `trace_nvme.py`, etc.) and `proxyclient/m1n1/trace/` constitute a category that none of the eight existing labels captures well. These files set up MMIO intercept handlers in the hypervisor to decode and print hardware register traffic. They are not tests (no assertions), not documentation (live instrumentation), not features (no new capability delivered to end users), not refactors. The closest label is `architectural scaffolding`, but the intent is research/observation, not extensibility. A proposed label: **reverse-engineering instrumentation** — tasks whose output is knowledge about undocumented hardware behavior rather than functional software capability.
